requirements.label: A full IB Diploma

officialWording.text: A secondary school diploma which is considered to be equivalent to the Dutch pre-university (VWO) diploma.

requirements.note: TU Delft asks for a diploma equivalent to the Dutch VWO. Nuffic, the recognition body, compares the full IB Diploma to a VWO diploma and DP Course Results only to vwo-deelcertificaten, so Course Results do not open a research university bachelor here. TU Delft adds that it does not accept the IB Career-related Programme. Nothing on tudelft.nl names DP Course Results, an IB Certificate or a partial IB at all; the category answer is that individual VWO subject certificates are not a basis for admission, which is the category Nuffic puts Course Results in.
requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you outright, but the only route TU Delft publishes is narrow, slow, and not on the pages an IB applicant is sent to. TU Delft admits on diplomas: it states that it "does not accept separate Dutch language certificates, English language certificates, or individual VWO subject certificates as a basis for admission", and individual VWO subject certificates — vwo-deelcertificaten — are exactly what Nuffic compares DP Course Results to. The published alternative is the colloquium doctum, which TU Delft documents only on its Dutch-diploma pages, and those pages send every IB holder away to the international-diploma route where the word never appears. To use it you must be 21 or older on the day the programme starts, show sufficient proficiency in Dutch — TU Delft states this applies to its English-taught programmes too — and meet the English requirement as well. No syllabus, deadline or fee is published: you arrange it by emailing contactcentre-esa@tudelft.nl with 'Colloquium Doctum' in the subject. Two things on the site look like routes and are not. The Dutch foundation-year programmes TU Delft lists sit inside a section that applies only to recognised refugees holding a Dutch residence permit, and TU Delft offers no foundation year of its own. The hbo propedeuse and associate degree route needs you to be admitted to a Dutch hogeschool first, and that asks for a havo, vwo or mbo-4 diploma, which brings you back to where you started. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the only route that reaches this programme at eighteen. One further route is national rather than this institution's, and it is the only one that produces the qualification itself instead of an exemption from it: the Dutch staatsexamen vwo. Anyone who registers may sit vwo subjects one at a time with DUO — registration for the 2027 examinations runs from 15 October to 31 December 2026, each subject costs 144 euro with a ceiling of 720 euro a year, and the certificates stay valid for ten years, so the package can be built up and exchanged for a vwo diploma at the end. No age limit applies, which is what makes it different from every colloquium doctum above, and Dutch law lets the College voor Toetsen en Examens grant you ontheffing from individual subjects on the strength of International Baccalaureate results — the one place in Dutch education law where the IB is named. The bill is linguistic: by statute the examinations are sat in Dutch.

alternativeRouteSummary.short: From 21: a colloquium doctum arranged by email, with Dutch required. At 18, only the full Diploma reaches it.

requirements.label: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL
requirements.note: TU Delft accepts only Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is not accepted at either level for any TU Delft programme.

requirements.label: Documented English proficiency

officialWording.text: You are required to pass one of the following language tests with the indicated minimum score requirement: TOEFL iBT 90 (internet based), or IELTS 6.5 (Academic version, Overall Band Score), or University of Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) or Certificate in Advanced English (CAE). [...] The following applicants are exempted from the English test requirement: [...] Applicants with a Surinam VWO, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate diploma, or European secondary school diploma (pre-university certificate) considered equivalent to the Dutch pre-university education, with English as a final examination subject. Please note that a 'pass' (sufficient score) for English is required on your secondary school certificate.

requirements.note: The exemption is not unconditional. TU Delft exempts IB Diploma holders who took English as a final examination subject and passed it. If English is not one of your six subjects, the exemption does not reach you and you would need IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 90 or Cambridge CAE/CPE.

officialRequirementsText.text: Earth, Climate and Technology (Previously Applied Earth Sciences)(English Stream) — Mathematics: AA HL + Physics HL + Chemistry: SL

notes: This is the one English-taught TU Delft bachelor that is not numerus clausus: it is absent from the university's own list of six capped programmes. So the deadline that binds you is 1 May 2027 rather than 15 January, and meeting the subject requirements is enough.
The programme was called Applied Earth Sciences until recently and TU Delft's own pages still carry both names. If you are searching Studielink or an older prospectus, look for either.
